resolved_findings.issue: Driver-owned pulse otherwise bypasses reset-core consumer ownership
resolved_findings.resolution: Hold reset-controller mutex, require reference list empty, retain mutex across the pulse; core get and put mutate that list under the same mutex.

resolved_findings.issue: Device RESET must not run during PS_RESET or BUSY transition
resolved_findings.resolution: Refuse preexisting bit12 or bit11; require ON and ACTUAL/TARGET15 before writing and through the held pulse.

resolved_findings.issue: A failed bus write may have committed, so cleanup cannot depend on successful writes
resolved_findings.resolution: Run cleanup from first attempted update onward and preserve operation_error separately from cleanup_error.

resolved_findings.issue: Cleanup originally claimed auto-PM remains inhibited although initial inhibit or final restore may fail after an uncertain write
resolved_findings.resolution: Cleanup attempts AUTO_ENABLE0 first and requires AUTO0/RESET0/DISABLE0 readback before policy restore; header explicitly preserves uncertainty if bus access fails.

resolved_findings.issue: Failed provider reads can overwrite the output supplied by a successful earlier poll sample
resolved_findings.resolution: Read into a temporary register value and only publish the value and its validity bit after success; independently replayed fault model poisons failed read output.

manual_review.lock_order: provider device mutex -> reset-controller mutex -> genpd spinlock -> MMIO regmap lock

limits: C model tests exclude kernel DT/device wrapper execution and actual inter-thread concurrency.
PMGR command readback does not establish reset coverage for ASC, GPU engines, UAT, caches, PHY or outstanding DMA.
No Apple native pointer-authentication or PHY initialization path is invoked or qualified.
All caller GPU/DMA backing remains retained; API success never authorizes freeing or reusing it.
Patch is an offline candidate for a new kernel build, not an API present in the current built-in provider.
Caller must own runtime-PM, serialize its resident worker, stop publication and use a sleepable context without holding the provider or domain locks.
